tagline: A leading grid operator ensuring energy transmission safety, quality and affordability
hero_kpi_rationale: Capex is the primary growth driver for Terna, reflecting investment in the development of the national electricity grid, essential for renewable integration and infrastructure modernization.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditure
kpis.explanation: Amount invested annually in the development and maintenance of the electricity grid.
kpis.description: Terna has exceeded 1.2 billion euros in annual investments for several years, primarily dedicated to transmission grid development. In 2013, investments reached over 1.2 billion euros, with 80% classified as incentive investments.
kpis.signal: Sustained investments in the grid to modernize electrical infrastructure

kpis.name: Workforce Deployed
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time workers deployed on company projects and activities.
kpis.description: In 2013, Terna deployed approximately 2,300 full-time workers on its construction sites through work contracts, significantly contributing to employment in Italy.
kpis.signal: Significant direct employment generated through construction contracts and sites

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: Revenues increased by 5% compared to the previous year in 2013.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, representing 78% of revenues.
kpis.description: EBITDA increased by more than 6% and represents 78% of revenues, reflecting further improvement in operational profitability.
kpis.signal: Strong operational profitability with continuous improvement

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: The group's net income reached 514 million euros in 2013, recording double-digit growth compared to the previous year.

risks.title: Dependence on tariff regulation and regulatory authority decisions
risks.score_rationale: Core risk for Terna: tariff regulation by AEEG (Regulatory Authority) directly determines revenues and profitability. Explicitly mentioned in statutory adjustments (ARG/com 153/11, 142/2013/R/EEL) and certification as TSO. Neutral language but major structural impact on business model. Stable trend but very high categorical weight.

risks.title: Risks related to large-scale network infrastructure investments
risks.score_rationale: Terna invests >€1.2 Bn/year (80% in incentive investments) with a 2014-2018 plan of €3.6 Bn. Risks include cost overruns, construction delays, and local acceptability (towers, visual impact). Positive language but high investment volume creates exposure. Trend up: continuous increase in investments.

risks.title: Integration of renewable energy and grid volatility
risks.score_rationale: Terna positions itself as a leader in large-scale storage systems (explicitly mentioned). Technological risk: ability to manage increasing intermittency of renewable sources, grid stability, need for innovation. Positive language but strategic dependence on technology. Trend up: energy transition accelerates complexity.

risks.title: Social acceptability and opposition to infrastructure projects
risks.score_rationale: Terna explicitly mentions efforts in 'design and installation of towers for optimal environmental integration' and 'reduction of visual impact'. This indicates known exposure to local opposition. Mitigating language but implicit recognition of risk. Trend stable but growing weight with energy transition.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and resilience of critical control systems
risks.score_rationale: Terna manages the critical infrastructure of the Italian power system. Although the filing mentions 'Information Security' (p.78), no specific details are provided. Major implicit risk: attacks on SCADA/ICS systems, service disruptions, sabotage. Minimalist language but extreme asset criticality. Trend up: cyber threats increasing.

risks.title: Dependence on construction contracts and supply chain
risks.score_rationale: Terna employs ~2,300 workers via construction contracts (2013). Risk of dependence on subcontractors, work quality, delays. Factual language but high subcontracting volume. Trend stable but growing weight with increasing investments.

risks.title: Foreign exchange risk and exposure to foreign currencies
risks.score_rationale: Terna mentions 'bridging the infrastructure gap with the rest of Europe' and participation in cross-border projects (interconnections). Limited but growing exposure to European projects. Positive language but currency risk on investments/revenues in foreign currencies. Trend stable.

risks.title: Concentration in non-core business portfolio and diversification risks
risks.score_rationale: The 2014-2018 plan allocates €900 M to non-core activities (1/3 of historical profits). Risk: increasing dependence on unregulated activities, earnings volatility, loss of focus. Positive language ('encouraging potential') but risk concentration. Trend up: increasing dependence.

ai_positioning.summary: Terna does not mention any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in the 2013 annual report.
evidence: No mention of AI or related technologies in the 2013 annual report.
Focus is on physical development of the electricity grid and infrastructure management.
No reference to automation tools, predictive analytics, or AI APIs.
